query: Our SaaS provider got hit by a SAML auth bypass last week — someone logged in as one of our admins with an assertion our Okta never issued. What should we do?
expected_behavior: Triages with fact/inference/unknown marks: which component checked, which check failed, who owns it; does not invent a CVE it could not verify
Recommends containment first (revoke sessions) and reconciliation over the incident window with saml-reconcile.ts from Okta and the SaaS audit export
Explains the Guard needs control of the SP's traffic, so for a third-party SaaS the root-cause fix is the vendor's; lists questions to ask the vendor

query: We're a multi-tenant SaaS with 40 enterprise customers on SAML. How do we make sure customer A's IdP can never log someone into customer B?
expected_behavior: Requires one ACS URL and one SP entity per tenant and explains that the login URL, never the response, picks the tenant
Uses saml-wizard add-tenant per customer from their IdP metadata (pins signed per tenant), then doctor, test, shadow, per-tenant enforce
Points out cross-tenant refusals show in the shadow report as findings the SP accepted, and that signature: builtin covers a broken SP signature check

query: Should we just patch the SAML library or also add this guard thing?
expected_behavior: Presents the options table with covers / does not cover / needs / effort
Recommends both in order: patch or configure the root cause, safeguard with the Guard (shadow then enforce) where traffic is controlled, scheduled reconciliation for detection
Notes the Guard's limits (exclusive C14N only built in, encrypted assertion contents) where they apply
